question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: Number of new passenger cars (Pkw) with first-time registration in Germany during September 2026, as reported by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in its monthly press release on vehicle registrations (Fahrzeugzulassungen). Counts new Pkw (personenkraftwagen) first registrations, domestic (Germany), al
target.cadence: monthly, typically released in the first week of the following month
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-09-05 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet; estimate must be built from prior-year seasonality, year-to-date momentum, order books, and policy/calendar effects. Working interpretation: KBA 'Neuzulassungen' of Pkw, domestic, full calendar month Sept

candidates.hypothesis: September new Pkw registrations follow a recurring seasonal pattern (September is typically a strong month due to post-summer and pre-Q4 push, and September 2025 was boosted by the end of the 2025 EV purchase incentive tail). Prior Septembers and the 2026 monthly run-rate anchor the level; September/adjacent-month ratio gives the seasonal multiplier.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registrations for September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, and monthly Jan-Aug 2026 (or latest available through Aug 2026), plus the September-to-August and September-to-annual ratios in recent years.

candidates.perspective: industry association (VDA) and automotive trade press
candidates.hypothesis: VDA monthly production/export and domestic order intake, plus trade-press reporting of incoming orders and dealer registrations, lead KBA registrations by weeks; a strong or weak order backlog in mid-2026 shifts September registrations proportionally.
candidates.data_to_find: VDA monthly domestic order intake and production for Pkw in 2026 (Jan-Aug), and any trade-press (Automobilwoche, Automobil Produktion) commentary on September 2026 registration expectations or order books.
search_hints: German car order intake 2026 VDA monthly

candidates.hypothesis: Published 2026 German passenger-car market forecasts (e.g., VDA, ifo, Euler Hermes, Bloomberg/Reuters consensus) give an annual total; applying the historical September share of the annual total yields a September 2026 estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Full-year 2026 German new Pkw registration forecasts published before 2026-09-05, and the historical September share of annual registrations (2015-2025).
search_hints: September share annual German car registrations

candidates.hypothesis: Policy changes (EV subsidy changes, CO2/fleet rules, company-car taxation) and macro conditions (interest rates, consumer confidence) shift the September 2026 level versus the seasonal baseline; measurable exposure (e.g., subsidy expiry dates, tax changes effective Q4 2026) can adjust the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Any German EV purchase incentive or company-car tax changes with effective dates around Q3/Q4 2026, and consumer-confidence/interest-rate indicators for mid-2026.

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 has a specific number of working days and no major holiday distortion; registrations scale with working days and month length, so a per-working-day rate from August 2026 times September working days gives a check.
candidates.data_to_find: Number of working days in September 2026 vs August 2026 in Germany, and the August 2026 KBA new Pkw total (if published before cutoff) or the latest monthly total.

candidates.hypothesis: German registrations move with EU-wide ACEA registrations; the German share of EU new Pkw registrations is fairly stable, so an EU September 2026 estimate (from ACEA or national data) times the German share gives a cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: ACEA monthly new passenger car registrations for the EU and Germany for 2025 and 2026 year-to-date, and the German share of EU registrations.

candidates.hypothesis: Domestic production plus imports minus exports minus inventory change approximates available vehicles for registration; a supply constraint or glut in mid-2026 would cap or boost September registrations.
candidates.data_to_find: German Pkw production, exports, and import volumes for 2026 (VDA/KBA), and any reported inventory or delivery-time data for mid-2026.

plan_notes: plan proposed 7 candidate directions in 6 categories; running 7 (budget cap 10)

extra_directions.hypothesis: A complete 2026 monthly KBA series (Jan-Aug) plus 2024/2025 monthly values would let series_auto and a September/adjacent-month seasonal ratio run properly; currently only scattered 2026 months are kept, so the own-history route is weak.
extra_directions.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registrations for every month of 2024, 2025 and Jan-Aug 2026 (exact counts).

extra_directions.hypothesis: Domestic order intake in June-August 2026 would sharpen the demand lead indicator for September; currently only Feb-Apr-May order data are kept, so the order-book route cannot be applied to the target month.
extra_directions.data_to_find: VDA monthly domestic and total order intake for June, July, August 2026.

extra_directions.hypothesis: The historical September share of the annual total (e.g. 2024, 2025) is needed to convert the VDA/ZDK annual forecast into a September estimate; without it the annual-share route relies on an assumption.
extra_directions.data_to_find: Annual 2024 and 2025 German new Pkw totals and September monthly values to compute the September share of the annual total.

methods.rationale: September 2025 total scaled by the 2026-vs-2025 momentum signal from August 2026 YoY; uses the latest observed YoY change as a proxy for September's YoY. Shared dependency: both rely on KBA monthly data; failure mode is that August momentum may not carry into September.

p50.role: August 2026 German new Pkw registrations (latest observed month)

methods.rationale: Latest observed month (August 2026, 212,563) times a September seasonal uplift. September 2025 was +13.7% MoM and September 2024 +5.8% MoM; 22 vs 21 working days supports a positive uplift. Failure mode: August 2026 may be unusually depressed or boosted.

p122.role: VDA 2026 annual German new Pkw registrations forecast (2.90mn)

methods.rationale: Annual forecast times September's share of the annual total. Uses VDA 2.90mn forecast; failure mode is that the forecast predates strong H1 and may be stale, and the September share is an assumption.

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

methods.rationale: September 2025 total scaled by a YoY growth factor reflecting 2026 momentum (H1 +6%, August +2.6%) tempered by VDA +2% full-year forecast. Failure mode: September 2025 was boosted by EV incentive tail, so YoY may be lower.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: 2026 YTD momentum is positive (H1 +6%, August +2.6% YoY, BEV +75% YoY) but VDA full-year forecast of +2% implies H2 moderation; September 2025 was itself boosted by EV incentive tail, so a modest YoY gain around +5% is central with wide range.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 demand continues 2026 momentum without a policy shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September 2026 collapse or boom (e.g. order intake crash or subsidy-driven surge).

assumptions.name: September 2026 seasonal multiplier vs August 2026
assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% MoM over August 2025; September 2024 was +5.8% MoM. September 2026 has 22 working days vs 21 in August 2026, supporting a positive MoM; central ~+10% with wide range.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 lacks the usual post-summer uplift.

assumptions.name: September share of annual registrations
assumptions.rationale: September is typically a strong month; with ~2.9mn annual total, a September share around 8-9% (roughly 235-260k) is consistent with 2025 September (235.5k) and 2024 (208.8k) relative to annual totals.
assumptions.applies_when: Annual forecast of ~2.9mn holds and September follows normal seasonality.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 share deviates strongly from historical norms.

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

assumptions.name: September 2026 seasonal multiplier vs August 2026

assumptions.name: September share of annual registrations

p50.role: August 2026 German new Pkw registrations (latest observed month)

previous_methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed month (August 2026, 212,563) and applies a September-over-August seasonal multiplier informed by 2024 and 2025 MoM changes and the extra working day. Shared dependency: p50 is the same KBA series as the target.

p122.role: VDA 2026 annual German new Pkw registrations forecast (2.90mn)

previous_methods.rationale: Converts the VDA 2026 annual forecast into a September estimate via the historical September share of the annual total. Failure mode: the VDA forecast may be stale relative to H2 2026 momentum, and the September share is an assumption.

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

previous_methods.rationale: Carries September 2025 forward by a YoY growth factor grounded in 2026 YTD +5% and August 2026 +2.6%, adjusted downward for the strong September 2025 base. Shared dependency: p1 is the same KBA series as the target.

previous_assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
previous_assumptions.rationale: 2026 YTD registrations running about +5% (p564: Jan-Aug 1,965,024, +5%), but August 2026 only +2.6% YoY (p51) and September 2025 was an unusually strong base boosted by the EV incentive tail (p1, p2). Modest positive factor with wide spread.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 demand continues the 2026 YTD trend but is dampened by the strong September 2025 base.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 order intake or early-month registrations collapsed or surged far outside the range.

previous_assumptions.name: September 2026 seasonal multiplier vs August 2026
previous_assumptions.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% MoM over August 2025 (p615) and September 2024 was +5.8% MoM over August 2024 (p16); September 2026 has one more working day than August 2026 (22 vs 21, p253/p289), supporting a positive but moderate multiplier.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The September-over-August seasonal uplift in 2026 resembles the 2024-2025 pattern.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 demand shock or calendar distortion.

previous_assumptions.name: September share of annual registrations
previous_assumptions.rationale: September 2025 (235,528, p1) was about 8.2% of the 2025 total (2,857,591, p549); September 2024 (208,848, p15) was about 7.4% of 2024 (2,817,331, p583). A share near 8-9% is consistent with September being a strong month.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 monthly distribution resembles recent years.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 monthly seasonality is materially different from 2024-2025.

methods.label: m2

p50.role: August 2026 German new Pkw registrations (latest observed month)

methods.rationale: Anchors on the latest observed month (August 2026, 212,563) and applies a September-over-August seasonal multiplier informed by 2024 and 2025 MoM changes and the extra working day. Shared dependency: p50 is the same KBA series as the target.

methods.label: m3

p122.role: VDA 2026 annual German new Pkw registrations forecast (2.90mn)

methods.rationale: Converts the VDA 2026 annual forecast into a September estimate via the historical September share of the annual total. Failure mode: the VDA forecast may be stale relative to H2 2026 momentum, and the September share is an assumption.

methods.label: m4

a1.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025

methods.rationale: Carries September 2025 forward by a YoY growth factor grounded in 2026 YTD +5% and August 2026 +2.6%, adjusted downward for the strong September 2025 base. Shared dependency: p1 is the same KBA series as the target.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m3: B3 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: this block is the median

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

kept.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025
kept.rationale: 2026 YTD registrations running about +5% (p564: Jan-Aug 1,965,024, +5%), but August 2026 only +2.6% YoY (p51) and September 2025 was an unusually strong base boosted by the EV incentive tail (p1, p2). Modest positive factor with wide spread.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 demand continues the 2026 YTD trend but is dampened by the strong September 2025 base.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 order intake or early-month registrations collapsed or surged far outside the range.

kept.name: September 2026 seasonal multiplier vs August 2026
kept.rationale: September 2025 was +13.7% MoM over August 2025 (p615) and September 2024 was +5.8% MoM over August 2024 (p16); September 2026 has one more working day than August 2026 (22 vs 21, p253/p289), supporting a positive but moderate multiplier.
kept.applies_when: The September-over-August seasonal uplift in 2026 resembles the 2024-2025 pattern.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 demand shock or calendar distortion.

kept.name: September share of annual registrations
kept.rationale: September 2025 (235,528, p1) was about 8.2% of the 2025 total (2,857,591, p549); September 2024 (208,848, p15) was about 7.4% of 2024 (2,817,331, p583). A share near 8-9% is consistent with September being a strong month.
kept.applies_when: The 2026 monthly distribution resembles recent years.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 monthly seasonality is materially different from 2024-2025.

published.note: not checked: backtest or scored question (as_of before today, or an official value is registered), so the target cannot have been published by as_of

Best estimate: [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]) for new Pkw first registrations in Germany, domestic, full calendar month September 2026, as to be reported by KBA.

Evidence: the combination is the median of [[n_methods]] blocks. m3 ([[m3_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m3_weight]]) carries forward September 2025 ([[p1_value]]) by a YoY factor of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]). m1 ([[m1_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m1_weight]]) applies a September-over-August multiplier of [[a2_value]] ([[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]]) to August 2026 ([[p50_value]]). m2 ([[m2_estimate]] [[unit]], weight [[m2_weight]]) scales the VDA annual forecast ([[p122_value]]) by a September share of [[a3_value]] ([[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]]).

Observed: the August 2026 level, September 2025 level and VDA annual forecast. Assumed: the growth factor, seasonal multiplier and September share. The blocks disagree by more than their own widths, so the interval was widened to cover all of them.

Main risk: the September 2025 base was unusually strong, so the YoY factor could be too high. Better evidence would be September 2026 order books or early-month registration data.

Unit of the estimate: [[unit_full]].

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025: [[a1_value]] [n], range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]; used by m3. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 order intake or early-month registrations collapsed or surged far outside the range.
- a2 September 2026 seasonal multiplier vs August 2026: [[a2_value]] [n], range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 demand shock or calendar distortion.
- a3 September share of annual registrations: [[a3_value]] [n], range [[a3_low]] to [[a3_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that 2026 monthly seasonality is materially different from 2024-2025.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p50 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m1_mc_p10]] to [[m1_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m1_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: p122 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m2_mc_p10]] to [[m2_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m2_width]] (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p1 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 [[m3_mc_p10]] to [[m3_mc_p90]]; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width [[m3_width]] (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: [[n_blocks]] block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: [[block1_value]] (width [[block1_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: [[block2_value]] (width [[block2_width]], Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B3 = m3: [[block3_value]] (width [[block3_width]], no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths [[blocks_rms_width]]; Birge ratio [[birge_ratio]] (above one, so the width is multiplied by it); final width [[final_width]]; the blocks are more than a factor of two apart; widened to cover every block.

Best estimate: 243 vehicle (80% model-based interval 1.615 to 244,870 vehicle) for new Pkw first registrations in Germany, domestic, full calendar month September 2026, as to be reported by KBA.

Evidence: the combination is the median of 3 blocks. m3 (243 vehicle, weight 100%) carries forward September 2025 (236 new passenger car registrations) by a YoY factor of 1.03 (range 0.9 to 1.18). m1 (232 vehicle, weight 0%) applies a September-over-August multiplier of 1.1 (0.7706 to 1.541) to August 2026 (213 new passenger car registrations). m2 (244,870 vehicle, weight 0%) scales the VDA annual forecast (2,900,000 new passenger car registrations) by a September share of 0.085 (0.05969 to 0.1194).

Observed: the August 2026 level, September 2025 level and VDA annual forecast. Assumed: the growth factor, seasonal multiplier and September share. The blocks disagree by more than their own widths, so the interval was widened to cover all of them.

Main risk: the September 2025 base was unusually strong, so the YoY factor could be too high. Better evidence would be September 2026 order books or early-month registration data.

Unit of the estimate: vehicle (new passenger car registrations; total for 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30).

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY growth factor vs September 2025: 1.03 [n], range 0.9 to 1.18; used by m3. Overturned by: Evidence that September 2026 order intake or early-month registrations collapsed or surged far outside the range.
- a2 September 2026 seasonal multiplier vs August 2026: 1.1 [n], range 0.7706 to 1.541 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 demand shock or calendar distortion.
- a3 September share of annual registrations: 0.085 [n], range 0.05969 to 0.1194 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that 2026 monthly seasonality is materially different from 2024-2025.

Method details (computed by code):
- m1 formula_mc: p50 * a2; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 156 to 341; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m2 formula_mc: p122 * a3; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 165,843 to 361,138; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.48 (Monte Carlo of the formula inputs)
- m3 formula_mc: p1 * a1; Monte Carlo P10 to P90 194 to 305; result unit (vehicle/month) * 1 month converted to vehicle; own 80% width x/÷1.38 (no error evidence, code's default width)
- Combination: 3 block(s), equal weight per block (methods whose inputs overlap by at least half form one block; backtest errors set widths, not weights): B1 = m1: 232 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B2 = m2: 244,870 (width x/÷1.48, Monte Carlo of the formula inputs); B3 = m3: 243 (width x/÷1.38, no error evidence, code's default width). Estimate = the median of the blocks.
- Interval: root mean square of the block widths x/÷1.44; Birge ratio 13.63 (above one, so the width is multiplied by it); final width x/÷150.53; the blocks are more than a factor of two apart; widened to cover every block.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
